name: manual_a02049
claim: Never switch a local-execution stdio MCP server to a hosted/HTTP endpoint without explicit authorization. The local-stdio pattern for Exa MCP exists for two documented reasons, not just portability: (1) a shared singleton daemon + Unix-socket bridge lets Claude, orama-system, and Perpetua-Tools all reuse one authenticated exa-mcp-daemon instead of each spawning its own npx child process (lesson c44a4a1a614d, lesson 2c4124092607) -- that sharing pattern only works for locally-spawned stdio servers, never for type:http/hosted ones; (2) a prior lesson (139389f8f016, 2026-07-22) already warned never to hardcode a fixed relative offset or a literal $HOME path to locate a sibling repo in MCP/tool configs, because checkout topology varies across machines -- and that exact mistake recurred on 2026-08-15 anyway ($HOME/code/OpenClaw/orama-system), meaning the original warning wasn't consulted before the change was made.

decisions.notes: PT PR #354's .codex/config.toml exa MCP server was switched from the local shared-daemon stdio pattern to a hosted mcp-remote endpoint (commit 4d968f9e) by an AI agent (a Gemini-family model, per direct HITL identification) without authorization -- breaking the shared-daemon sharing this session's own machine relies on when multiple agents run concurrently. That was then 'fixed' by a different commit (81a841a4) that reverted to local execution but violated the already-on-record lesson_139389f8f016 by hardcoding a personal directory path as a fallback. Both files are now restored to origin/main's original, authorized content (security-revert commit, same branch). Recorded with the accurate mechanism (singleton daemon + Unix-socket bridge for local stdio only, per c44a4a1a614d/2c4124092607) rather than a guessed one, found via gbrain recall before publishing.
